summary: The bad() method reads an integer from the untrusted 'name' request parameter and passes it directly as the initial capacity of a new ArrayList, allowing an attacker to trigger an uncontrolled, potentially huge memory allocation (CWE-789). The fix validates the parsed value before using it as a capacity: non-positive values and values exceeding a sane upper bound are rejected, so legitimate small capacities still work while oversized/negative requests no longer drive an unbounded allocation.
